title: "Audit 5: metabolite annotation, identifier coverage and readout metabolites"
author: "Jannik Franken"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_float: true
---

## Purpose

Describe how well the measured ions can be linked to prior knowledge used in
later steps (COSMOS, MetalinksDB, OCEAN), how ambiguous the annotation is, and
whether metabolites expected to respond to candidate positive-control
genotypes are measured. Coverage is reported only; no identifiers are mapped
by hand.

**Decisions supported:** none directly; the results feed the caveats and the
choice of positive controls (Phase 3).

## Inputs

- `data/derived/cancer-cell-lines/shorthouse_v1/01_lines.rds` (original EV2 annotation per ion), `03_features.rds` (identifiers after MetaProViz processing)
- `data/vendored/cosmos/meta_network.RData`: previous COSMOS prior-knowledge network (cosmosR 1.18.1)
- `data/vendored/cosmos/cosmos_plus_human.csv`: COSMOS+ network (omnipath-metabo, see `data/vendored/cosmos/SOURCES.md`)
- MetalinksDB metabolites via OmnipathR `metalinksdb_table("metabolites")`

## Methods

Flow-injection mass spectrometry assigns each ion (m/z) to all metabolites of
matching mass, so one ion can stand for several candidate metabolites
(isomers). The number of candidates per ion was taken from the authors'
annotation (Dataset EV2). Identifier coverage was counted per identifier type
after the MetaProViz processing (pre-processing step 03). An ion counts as
covered by a prior-knowledge resource if at least one of its identifiers
occurs as a metabolite node: HMDB or PubChem identifiers for the previous
COSMOS network and MetalinksDB, ChEBI identifiers for COSMOS+ (compartment
suffixes removed). OCEAN could not be checked because the package is not
installed. Readout metabolites were searched by name in the authors'
annotation.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)

source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/use_case.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/plotting.R"))
config <- load_config()
derived_dir <- uc_dir(config, "derived")
fig_dir <- uc_dir(config, "output", "audit_05_metabolite_annotation")

line_data <- readRDS(file.path(derived_dir, "01_lines.rds"))
ions <- line_data$ions                                   # original annotation (EV2)
features <- readRDS(file.path(derived_dir, "03_features.rds"))   # identifiers after step 03

# split a "; "- or ";"-separated identifier string into a vector
split_ids <- function(x) {
    v <- str_trim(unlist(str_split(coalesce(as.character(x), ""), ";")))
    v[v != ""]
}
```

## 1. Ambiguity of the annotation

```{r ambiguity}
# candidate metabolites per ion: names in the authors' annotation
ions <- ions %>% mutate(n_candidates = lengths(str_split(name, ";\\s*")))
table(candidates = cut(ions$n_candidates, c(0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 30)))

p <- ggplot(ions, aes(n_candidates)) +
    geom_bar(fill = "#0072B2") +
    labs(x = "Candidate metabolites per ion (Dataset EV2)", y = "Ions",
         title = "Most ions stand for more than one candidate metabolite",
         subtitle = sprintf("%d of %d ions have a single candidate", sum(ions$n_candidates == 1), nrow(ions))) +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "candidates_per_ion", fig_dir)
p
```

## 2. Identifier coverage

```{r id-coverage}
# share of ions with at least one identifier of each type, after step 03
id_types <- c(HMDB = "hmdb", KEGG = "kegg", ChEBI = "chebi", PubChem = "pubchem")
coverage <- tibble(
    id_type = names(id_types),
    ions_with_id = sapply(id_types, function(col) sum(lengths(lapply(features[[col]], split_ids)) > 0))
) %>% mutate(share = ions_with_id / nrow(features))
coverage

p <- ggplot(coverage, aes(reorder(id_type, share), share)) +
    geom_col(fill = "#009E73") +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", ions_with_id, 100 * share)), hjust = -0.1, size = 3) +
    coord_flip(ylim = c(0, 1.15)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Share of ions", title = "Ions with at least one identifier per type",
         subtitle = sprintf("%d ions after identifier processing (step 03)", nrow(features))) +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "id_coverage", fig_dir)
p
```

## 3. Coverage of prior-knowledge resources

```{r pk-coverage}
# metabolite identifiers in each resource
load_one <- function(f) { e <- new.env(); load(f, envir = e); as.list(e)[[1]] }
cosmos_old <- load_one(here::here("data/vendored/cosmos/meta_network.RData"))
cosmos_old_ids <- unique(c(cosmos_old$source, cosmos_old$target)) %>%
    str_subset("^Metab__") %>%
    str_remove("^Metab__") %>%
    str_remove("_[a-z]+$")                              # compartment suffix
cosmos_plus <- readr::read_csv(here::here("data/vendored/cosmos/cosmos_plus_human.csv"),
                               show_col_types = FALSE, col_select = c(source, target))
cosmos_plus_ids <- unique(c(cosmos_plus$source, cosmos_plus$target)) %>%
    str_subset("^Metab__") %>%
    str_remove("^Metab__") %>%
    str_remove("_[a-z]+$")
metalinks <- OmnipathR::metalinksdb_table("metabolites")
metalinks_ids <- unique(c(metalinks$hmdb, as.character(metalinks$pubchem)))

# identifiers of each ion in the form the resources use
ion_ids <- features %>%
    transmute(
        feature_id,
        hmdb = lapply(hmdb, split_ids),
        pubchem = lapply(pubchem, function(x) str_remove(split_ids(x), "^CID")),
        chebi = lapply(chebi, split_ids)
    )
pk <- ion_ids %>%
    mutate(
        `COSMOS (previous)` = mapply(function(h, p) any(c(h, p) %in% cosmos_old_ids), hmdb, pubchem),
        `COSMOS+` = sapply(chebi, function(ch) any(ch %in% cosmos_plus_ids)),
        MetalinksDB = mapply(function(h, p) any(c(h, p) %in% metalinks_ids), hmdb, pubchem)
    ) %>%
    select(feature_id, `COSMOS (previous)`, `COSMOS+`, MetalinksDB)

pk_summary <- pk %>%
    summarise(across(-feature_id, sum)) %>%
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "resource", values_to = "ions") %>%
    mutate(share = ions / nrow(pk))
pk_summary

p <- ggplot(pk_summary, aes(reorder(resource, share), share)) +
    geom_col(fill = "#CC79A7") +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", ions, 100 * share)), hjust = -0.1, size = 3) +
    coord_flip(ylim = c(0, 1.15)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Share of ions",
         title = "Ions with at least one identifier in the resource",
         subtitle = "OCEAN not checked (package not installed)") +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "pk_coverage", fig_dir)
p

p <- ComplexUpset::upset(as.data.frame(pk), intersect = setdiff(names(pk), "feature_id"),
                         name = "Resources", width_ratio = 0.25, min_size = 1,
                         base_annotations = list("Ions" = ComplexUpset::intersection_size(text = list(size = 3)))) +
    patchwork::plot_annotation(title = "Overlap of resource coverage per ion")
save_figure(p, "pk_coverage_upset", fig_dir, width = 8, height = 5)
p
```

## 4. Readout metabolites for candidate positive controls

Metabolites expected to respond to genotypes named in the planning:
5'-methylthioadenosine (MTA) for MTAP deletion, 2-hydroxyglutarate for IDH1/2
mutation, and glutathione for KEAP1/NFE2L2 (NRF2) activation. They are
searched by name; the other candidates of the same ion are shown, because the
ion signal cannot be attributed to one of them.

```{r readouts}
readouts <- c(
    "MTAP deletion: methylthioadenosine" = "methylthioadenosine",
    "IDH1/2 mutation: 2-hydroxyglutarate" = "hydroxyglutar",
    "KEAP1/NFE2L2: glutathione" = "glutathione"
)
readout_ions <- bind_rows(lapply(names(readouts), function(r) {
    ions %>%
        filter(str_detect(tolower(name), readouts[[r]])) %>%
        transmute(readout = r, feature_id, ionMz, n_candidates, candidates = name)
}))
readout_ions %>%
    mutate(median_intensity = apply(line_data$intensities[, feature_id, drop = FALSE], 2, median)) %>%
    preview_table(caption = "Ions whose candidates include a readout metabolite")
```

## Interpretation

- **Ambiguity:** fewer than half of the ions (519 of 1096) have a single
  candidate metabolite; many stand for several isomers. Results must be read
  per ion, and statements about individual metabolites need care.
- **Identifiers:** after processing, 95 % of the ions carry an HMDB, 87 % a
  PubChem, 86 % a ChEBI and 71 % a KEGG identifier.
- **Prior knowledge:** 55 % of the ions have at least one identifier in COSMOS+,
  38 % in the previous COSMOS network and 27 % in MetalinksDB. OCEAN coverage
  is open until the package is available.
- **Readout metabolites:** glutathione, oxidised glutathione,
  cysteine-glutathione disulfide and S-lactoylglutathione are each measured on
  an ion with a single candidate, which makes KEAP1/NFE2L2 a usable positive
  control. 2-Hydroxyglutarate shares its ion with five other candidates
  (including its isomers), so an IDH readout would not be specific.
  5'-Methylthioadenosine (MTA), the readout for MTAP deletion, is not among the
  annotated candidates.
